assumptions: No arrival context was given. Assumed Sophie & James found the post through a Google search for 'milestone birthday' while browsing Wedded Wonderland, because James's mum turns 60 the year before their wedding and they are thinking of a family weekend away.
HTML comments (image slots, META, fact markers) are treated as invisible.

Business details (fees, commissions, on the ground support, transfers, room blocks, Wedded Privileges, phone lines) are deliberately deferred, so I did not mark them as gaps or suggest edits for them.
self_qa follows envelope.schema.json (an object with checks and confidence). Confidence is also repeated at the top level as the orchestrator asked.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (Sydney, early research, wary of clichés, hidden costs and hard sells)
No invented brand facts; anything the page doesn't say is in unanswered_questions
Every suggested edit's old text is an exact, unique substring of 05-draft.md
No suggested edit adds prices, fees, commissions, vendor names, statistics words or em dashes, or asks how the fee is worked out
Did not invent problems; positives recorded where the draft earned them

open_questions.question: The concierge paragraph says Wedded Concierge quotes 'in AUD for Australian couples'. A birthday host is often one person or a family, not a couple. Does that AUD claim apply to any Australian client? If yes, the brand owner could reword it. I have not suggested an edit because it would widen a brand claim.
Is there a real celebration (venue and date) or a related post the page could link to? We trust real examples, and the page has none.

first_impression.reaction: Calm and grown up, no 'fabulous fiesta' stuff. 'Would they rather be fussed over at home or taken somewhere new?' is exactly what we're arguing about for James's mum, so I kept going. I skimmed the ideas by style and slowed down at the home vs destination table and the travel section.

journey.quote: The celebrations that land well start with the guest of honour.
journey.reaction: Good starting point, and nothing about dream days or magic. It sounds like someone who has actually done this.

journey.quote: A candle is an open flame and can easily ignite anything combustible nearby, so keep the area around each one clear of linen, florals and paper, and use sturdy holders made of material that cannot burn, as the
journey.reaction: We know candles are hot. This reads like a fire brigade pamphlet in a lifestyle article and feels a bit beneath us. Keep the practical point and lose the lecture.

journey.section: A long lunch or garden party
journey.quote: Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before going outside and again every two hours.
journey.reaction: Now it's a school excursion note. The sunscreen basket is a nice touch for older relatives, but the application instructions make it feel less premium.
Like it. That's how we'd want a weekend away to feel, not a schedule of activities.

journey.quote: Plan for comfort first: short journeys, rooms without stairs where needed, and one evening when everyone sits down together.
journey.reaction: This is the grandparents worry in one line. It makes me think they've dealt with older guests before.

journey.section: A party at home or a destination weekend
journey.quote: There is a middle path too: a party at home for the wider circle, then a few days away with the closest few.
journey.reaction: An honest trade-off, and the table is clear. It doesn't push us towards the expensive option, which I trust more.

journey.section: Choose the date and book the anchor event
journey.quote: Who holds the liquor licence, who serves, are bar staff trained in responsible service of alcohol, and is BYO allowed?
journey.reaction: Insider stuff. I'd never have thought to ask who holds the licence. This list is the most useful part of the page, and I'd forward it to James's sister.

journey.quote: For a destination weekend, for example, start several months ahead so guests can plan leave and flights.
journey.reaction: 'Several months' is vague. I get that it depends, but a rough range would help me plan. Not a deal breaker.

journey.section: Choosing a place guests can reach
journey.quote: Before you commit, read the destination's travel advice on [Smartraveller](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/before-you-go), which recommends you subscribe to the destinations you're visiting, including where you're transiting through.
journey.reaction: Useful advice, but the sentence is clunky. I had to read it twice.

journey.quote: Declare everything upfront, including pre-existing health conditions, or the policy may be void.
journey.reaction: Exactly what James's grandmother needs to hear. Specific and sourced, and it makes the brand feel careful.

journey.section: Where everyone stays and one hosted dinner
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans milestone birthdays through the same Wedded Advisor process: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person and AUD quotes speak to two of our fears: no one being accountable, and currency surprises. 'Couples' jars a little here, since it's his mum's birthday.

journey.section: Planning a milestone birthday with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: A milestone birthday brings people together from near and far, and it deserves the care of any celebration that does.
journey.reaction: Filler. It says nothing, and after a page of specifics it reads like a brochure sign-off.

journey.section: Planning a milestone birthday with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Good. Knowing the fee is agreed in writing first takes the edge off the hidden costs worry.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Concierge plan a party at home in Sydney, or only birthdays that involve travel?
Is there a real birthday or family celebration they've planned, with a venue and date, that we could look at?
Roughly how far ahead should we start a destination weekend if most guests are flying from Australia? 'Several months' could mean three or nine.

turn_offs_found.quote: A candle is an open flame and can easily ignite anything combustible nearby
turn_offs_found.why: Patronising safety-pamphlet tone that cheapens an otherwise considered page.

turn_offs_found.quote: A milestone birthday brings people together from near and far, and it deserves the care of any celebration that does.
turn_offs_found.why: Generic marketing line where we expected a concrete reason to talk to them.

would_share_with: James's sister, who would co-host his mum's 60th (the venue questions list and the travel insurance reminders)

cta_reaction.why: It's low pressure, which I like, and 'fee agreed in writing' helps. But for a birthday we'd probably organise it ourselves unless it turns into a full family trip, and I'd want to see one real example first.

top_3_changes: Cut the candle and sunscreen instructions down to one practical line each. They read like a council pamphlet and drag the premium feel down.
Swap the generic closing opener for a line that connects a travelling birthday to the planning they already do for destination weddings.
Rewrite the Smartraveller subscription sentence so it reads cleanly on the first pass.

suggested_edits.old: A candle is an open flame and can easily ignite anything combustible nearby, so keep the area around each one clear of linen, florals and paper, and use sturdy holders made of material that cannot burn, as the
suggested_edits.new: Keep linen, florals and paper well clear of every candle and use sturdy holders that cannot burn, as the
suggested_edits.reason: Same safety point without the lecturing tone. To us it reads like a fire brigade pamphlet, which feels beneath a premium brand.

suggested_edits.old: Leave SPF50+ sunscreen and hats at the entrance. Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before going outside and again every two hours.
suggested_edits.new: Leave SPF50+ sunscreen and hats at the entrance so guests can reapply through the afternoon.
suggested_edits.reason: The hosting gesture is the useful part. The application instructions sound like a school note and add no value for us. The editor should check whether fact_03 still needs to appear.

suggested_edits.old: which recommends you subscribe to the destinations you're visiting, including where you're transiting through.
suggested_edits.new: and subscribe to updates for each place on the route, including transit stops, as Smartraveller recommends.
suggested_edits.reason: The current wording is clunky and took two reads. The meaning and the source stay the same.

suggested_edits.old: A milestone birthday brings people together from near and far, and it deserves the care of any celebration that does.
suggested_edits.new: When guests are travelling from several places, planning a birthday weekend looks a lot like planning a small destination wedding.
suggested_edits.reason: Swaps a filler line for a concrete reason to read on. It adds no brand facts.
